core.recovery.already_matches: The key already matches, nothing to do
core.hook.invalid_json: ~/.claude/settings.json is not valid JSON (%{error}); nothing was changed so your configuration is not overwritten. Please fix it first, then install
core.recovery.recreated: Recreated the empty folder %{dir} (~/.claude was not touched)
core.recovery.switched: Switched to %{dir} (this tool does not index sessions by folder, so the storage needs no change)
core.recovery.linked: Created a symlink under %{key}/ pointing to the original session record
core.recovery.parent_missing: The parent folder does not exist either: %{dir}. This looks like more than a deleted project folder (an external drive may not be mounted, or a whole parent folder was moved), so the whole folder tree was not created for you. Mount the drive, or use "Point to a new location" instead
doctor.tool.title: %{name} command
doctor.tool.found_no_version: Found at %{path}, but `--version` did not answer (timeout or error)
doctor.tool.fix_version: Run `%{name} --version` in a terminal; if it fails there too, reinstall it.
doctor.tool.optional_missing: Not detected (fine if you do not use it)
doctor.tool.none_found: Not detected, and none of the supported tools was found
doctor.tool.fix_install: Install at least one of Claude Code, Codex or opencode. If it is installed in a place we do not look, running it in makit's own terminal still works.
doctor.path.title: PATH of the app vs your login shell
doctor.path.same: Every folder of your login shell's PATH that holds a supported tool is also on the app's PATH
doctor.path.differs: Not on the app's PATH but on your shell's: %{dirs}
doctor.path.fix: Normally harmless: terminals opened inside makit use your shell's PATH. It only matters for things the app starts itself.
doctor.path.unknown: Could not read the login shell's PATH (no $SHELL, or it did not answer in time)
doctor.proxy.title: Proxy environment variables
doctor.proxy.fix: Use the form scheme://host:port (for example http://127.0.0.1:7890) and make the upper- and lower-case variables agree. Remove variables you no longer use; a stale proxy is a common cause of failed requests.
doctor.data.title: makit data folder (~/.claude/makit)
doctor.data.missing: Does not exist yet (it is created on first use)
doctor.data.fix: Check the folder's owner and permissions (`ls -ld ~/.claude/makit`); makit cannot save its settings or archive until it is writable.
doctor.hook.socket.title: Notification hook channel
doctor.hook.socket.missing: The socket %{path} does not exist: the hook server did not start
doctor.hook.socket.stale: %{path} exists but nothing answers: a leftover from a crashed instance
doctor.hook.socket.fix: Quit every makit instance and start it again. If it keeps failing, copy the diagnostics from Settings and open an issue.
doctor.hook.socket.unsupported: Not available on this platform yet
doctor.hook.config.title: Claude Code hook configuration
doctor.hook.config.none: No makit hook in ~/.claude/settings.json: approval and finished notifications from Claude Code will not arrive
doctor.hook.config.partial: Only %{n} of %{total} makit hooks are installed
doctor.hook.config.invalid: ~/.claude/settings.json is not valid JSON; makit will not touch it
doctor.hook.config.fix: Settings -> Notifications -> Install Claude Code hook. If the file is invalid, fix it by hand first.
doctor.dir.missing: Does not exist (that tool was never used)
doctor.dir.fix: On macOS give makit Full Disk Access (System Settings -> Privacy & Security), or check the folder's permissions.
doctor.jsonl.title: Claude session files
doctor.jsonl.ok: The %{n} newest files all start with valid JSON
doctor.jsonl.broken: %{broken} of the %{n} newest files do not start with valid JSON
doctor.jsonl.fix: Those sessions are skipped in the list. Usually an interrupted write; the file can be removed if you do not need it.
doctor.opencode.title: opencode session database
doctor.opencode.fix_schema: Probably a newer opencode than makit understands; its sessions are not shown. Update makit.
doctor.opencode.fix_open: Check the file's permissions and that no other tool holds it exclusively.
